newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt all-share index inches up to 15th record.
newsitem.headline: Egypt all-share index inches up to 15th record.

text.p: Egypt's all-share index broke all records and the 400 point level on Thursday with more than half the day's traded stocks gaining the five percent maximum stipulated by the Capital Market Authority (CMA).
The CMA index inched 0.51 percent higher to close at 401.64, its 15th record level in as many trading days.
Turnover was a heavy 223.35 million pounds ($65.69 million) swollen by the state's sale of 2.896 million shares or 48 percent in Nile Cotton Ginning to strategic investors for 128.036 million pounds.
The state's Holding Company for Cotton and International Trading had offered at least 1.2 million of the six million shares in the company.

Trade in newly privatised Misr Free Shops also contributed 15.24 million pounds to turnover and the stock closed one pound higher at 43 pounds. Rarely traded firm Lecico Ceramic Tiles and Sanitary Ware added another 12.37 million pounds but shares ended unchanged at 6,090 pounds.
The popular cement and milling shares made up most of the remaining trade but their prices were mixed.
Central Egypt Flour Mills was the best performing in its sector, rising 3.74 pounds to 78.71 in trading worth almost 4.6 million pounds.
But profit taking brought down the prices of Central and West Delta Flour Mills 6.6 pounds to 125.4 and East Delta Flour Mills also shed 4.77 pounds to 94.75.
Among the cement firms, Amriya Cement was the biggest gainer and the most actively traded, with shares rising 2.7 pounds to 93 in deals worth more than 8.7 million pounds.
Heavy trading continued in privatised al-Ahram Beverages, also known as Pyramids Breweries, and shares ended 4.98 pounds higher at 104.65.

Egyptian brokerage firm El-Rashad Securities Brokerage said the U.S.-based Luxor Group, which owns a majority in the monopoly brewer, was going to transfer 70 percent of its holdings into a global depositary receipt offering.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 665.27 points from 662.44 points on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 265.93 from 264.43 points.
Out of the 79 shares traded, 43 gained, 19 lost and 17 ended the day unchanged.
